ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AC = 10$, the perpendicular bisector of $AB$ intersects $AB$ at point $M$ and intersects $AC$ at point $D$. The perimeter of $\triangle BDC$ is $18$. What is the length of $BC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $MN$ is the perpendicular bisector of $AB$,\\
then $BD = AD$,\\
thus the perimeter of $\triangle BDC = BD + CD + BC = AD + CD + BC = AC + BC = 18$,\\
since $AC = 10$,\\
therefore $BC = \boxed{8}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is above, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right; D is located on side AC, and BD is connected; an oblique line labeled M, N passes through D and intersects AB, and a right-angle mark is drawn at the intersection point, indicating that this line is perpendicular to AB. The problem statement explains that this line is the perpendicular bisector of AB. Reasoning: Because D is on the perpendicular bisector of AB, the distances from D to the two points A and B are equal, namely BD = AD. The perimeter of triangle BDC is BD + DC + BC = 18. Replacing BD with AD gives AD + DC + BC = 18. Since D is on AC, AD + DC = AC = 10. Therefore 10 + BC = 18, solving gives BC = 8.
